{
  "concerns": [
    {
      "id": "SKP-001",
      "concern": "Canonicalization approach is internally inconsistent (RFC 8785 JCS claimed, but multiple sections still specify jq -S -c).",
      "severity": "CRITICAL",
      "severity_score": 930,
      "why_matters": "Hashes/signatures will diverge across implementations if canonicalization is not exactly one algorithm. This can cause false chain-breaks, failed signature verification, and audit system collapse.",
      "location": "§2.2 (Canonical JSON), §3.3 (canonical serialization), Appendix A/B references to jq -S -c",
      "recommendation": "Define one normative canonicalization algorithm and remove contradictory references. Add MUST-level test vectors and fail CI if any implementation byte output differs."
    },
    {
      "id": "SKP-002",
      "concern": "Single-machine assumption conflicts with stated system vision of operator-absent multi-operator/multi-repo workflows.",
      "severity": "CRITICAL",
      "severity_score": 900,
      "why_matters": "Real teams will operate across multiple machines/CI runners; current design hard-refuses writes via fingerprint checks, risking operational deadlock and user workarounds that bypass safety.",
      "location": "§1.1 (system overview), §1.7 and §1.7.1 (single-machine + cross-host refusal)",
      "recommendation": "Either narrow product claims to same-machine explicitly everywhere or implement a minimal multi-host coordination strategy before rollout (canonical writer, merge protocol, shared trust-store sync)."
    },
    {
      "id": "SKP-003",
      "concern": "Root-of-trust bootstrap and rotation process is underspecified and operationally brittle (single maintainer offline key bottleneck).",
      "severity": "HIGH",
      "severity_score": 780,
      "why_matters": "If maintainer unavailable or root key lost/compromised, trust-store updates stall and audit verification may halt project operation.",
      "location": "§1.9.3.1 trust-store root of trust",
      "recommendation": "Add formal root key ceremony, escrow/recovery process, quorum-based alternate signers, and explicit business-continuity runbook with tested drills."
    },
    {
      "id": "SKP-004",
      "concern": "Performance/SLO targets are not credible against required cryptographic + schema-validation write path and frequent session-start processing.",
      "severity": "HIGH",
      "severity_score": 740,
      "why_matters": "p95/p99 goals may fail under realistic log sizes and slower laptops/CI, causing perceived flakiness and pressure to disable security checks.",
      "location": "§1.4.1 audit write path, §1.8 scalability, changelog mention of write-path SLOs",
      "recommendation": "Benchmark with worst-case payloads and long chains; define degradation behavior; introduce incremental verification/indexing and explicit perf budgets per primitive."
    },
    {
      "id": "SKP-005",
      "concern": "Prompt-injection defenses rely on heuristics and turn-based provenance assumptions that attackers can bypass.",
      "severity": "HIGH",
      "severity_score": 760,
      "why_matters": "Tool-call gating tied to first-N-turn heuristics and pattern detection can miss delayed, obfuscated, or indirect injections, enabling unauthorized actions.",
      "location": "§1.9.3.2 layered defense and deny-by-default resolver",
      "recommendation": "Enforce provenance taint through full conversation DAG, not turn window heuristics; require explicit operator confirmation for all mutating/exfiltrating tools when untrusted context is present."
    },
    {
      "id": "SKP-006",
      "concern": "Backup/recovery still accepts up to 7-day data loss for untracked critical logs, conflicting with forensic integrity goals.",
      "severity": "HIGH",
      "severity_score": 710,
      "why_matters": "L1/L2 chain segments can be irrecoverably lost between snapshots, undermining claims of complete auditable decision history.",
      "location": "§3.7 Backup and Recovery (weekly snapshot, RPO=7 days)",
      "recommendation": "Move critical logs to tracked or near-real-time append replication; reduce RPO to <=24h (or near-zero) and validate restore procedures in CI."
    },
    {
      "id": "SKP-007",
      "concern": "Integration complexity is underestimated across seven primitives with optional composition and only five tested tier combinations.",
      "severity": "HIGH",
      "severity_score": 700,
      "why_matters": "Unsupported but possible config permutations can behave unpredictably in production; warn-mode tier enforcement allows risky combos to run anyway.",
      "location": "§1.4/§1.6 composition model, §1.4.1 tier validator, §7.2.4 tier tests",
      "recommendation": "Either hard-refuse unsupported tiers by default or dramatically expand compatibility matrix tests; add contract tests for every primitive-pair interaction."
    },
    {
      "id": "SKP-008",
      "concern": "Identity verification model is weak/optional and can produce false confidence in handoff/trust decisions.",
      "severity": "MEDIUM",
      "severity_score": 560,
      "why_matters": "Optional git/gpg checks and warn modes permit unverified actors to appear in key workflows, reducing non-repudiation and enabling impersonation in shared environments.",
      "location": "§1.4.1 Operator Identity Library, §1.9.1 Authentication, §5.8 L6 strict/warn modes",
      "recommendation": "Set strict identity verification defaults for sensitive operations; require cryptographic identity for trust changes and handoff authorship in production mode."
    },
    {
      "id": "SKP-009",
      "concern": "L2 billing uncertainty logic and provider-lag rules are complex and likely to cause frequent false halts or operator override fatigue.",
      "severity": "MEDIUM",
      "severity_score": 540,
      "why_matters": "Overly conservative fail-closed behavior without robust auto-reconciliation can repeatedly stop autonomous cycles, reducing system usefulness and encouraging unsafe bypasses.",
      "location": "§1.5.3 L2 state model, §5.4 reconciliation and uncertainty thresholds",
      "recommendation": "Calibrate thresholds with production telemetry, implement bounded auto-reconcile with safeguards, and define clear operator UX for temporary degraded operation."
    },
    {
      "id": "SKP-010",
      "concern": "Timeline risk remains severe: scope includes heavy cross-cutting infra plus 7 primitives in 6-10 weeks despite prior critical schedule warnings.",
      "severity": "MEDIUM",
      "severity_score": 590,
      "why_matters": "Underestimated effort can force late de-scoping or rushed security/integration work, creating long-term technical debt and unstable delivery.",
      "location": "§8 Development Phases, §9 Risk R11",
      "recommendation": "Rebaseline with explicit critical path, reduce initial scope (ship fewer primitives first), and gate later primitives on measured completion and stability metrics."
    }
  ],
  "summary": "10 concerns identified, 2 CRITICAL"
}
